messages:
vivian: Proposal: change external SIEM export default retention to 45d (was 90). Need RBAC gating, KMS JIT unwrap, and a tight forensic_hold flow. @raj @kelsey
raj: 45d seems like a reasonable compromise between forensics needs and minimization. We must pair this with a simple extension path and explicit audit trail.
kelsey: RBAC suggestion: scoped roles `audit:export:requester`, `audit:export:approver`, `audit:export:runner`. Only a small allowlist of svc accounts get `runner`. Approver toggles approved=true on the request record.
vivian: KMS design: UnwrapProxy validates request.approved && request.forensic_hold==false, then calls KMS:Decrypt with EncryptionContext.export_id and returns an ephemeral unwrap token (TTL=12m) to the runner. All decrypts log to CloudTrail and we emit a SIEM event `export.unseal` (export_id, approver, executor).
legal-zoe: Legal ok with 45d for routine partner handbacks. Forensic_hold must require both legal + security signoff; while held, automated unwraps are blocked and the request metadata is marked immutable. Release requires documented justification and recorded approver IDs.
raj: DLP gating: add `contains_sensitive` checkbox and `data_type` enum (PII/Auth/Payment/Other). If true, write export output to a quarantined bucket path and run DLP scrub before final upload; approver must re-approve post-DLP.
vivian: Minimal CLI examples:
```
redwood export create --scope "auth*:2026-03-21..2026-03-22" --retention 45 --justification "partner triage" --requester vivian@redwood.ai
redwood export approve --id EXP-2026-5001 --approver kelsey@redwood.ai
```
audit-bot: ticket SEC-2026-5501 created; status: triage; https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2026-5501
